paper.title: Remember Me, Refine Me: A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution
paper.central_claim: ReMe, a three-phase procedural memory framework (multi-faceted distillation, context-adaptive reuse, utility-based refinement), establishes a new state of the art in agent memory on BFCL-V3 and AppWorld, and shows a memory-scaling effect: Qwen3-8B with ReMe outperforms larger memoryless Qwen3-14B.

8B + ReMe(dynamic): avg Avg@4 34.94, avg Pass@4 55.03.

A-Mem baseline falls below No Memory on AppWorld (12.95 vs 14.97) - baseline strength is uncertain.

evidence.support_explanation: Selective-addition gate for new entries.

evidence.quote: we limit the maximum number of self-reflections to 3
evidence.support_explanation: Failure-aware reflection retries up to 3 extra trials per failed task.

evidence.quote: which increments by 1 each time its recall contributes to a successful task completion
evidence.support_explanation: Utility credit: any recall in a successful task adds 1, regardless of co-retrieved entries.

evidence.quote: removes any experience whose average utility across all its past recalls falls below a predefined threshold
evidence.support_explanation: Utility-based deletion rule (retrieved >= alpha=5 times, u/f <= beta=0.5).
Adding deletion: +0.17 Avg@4, +3.34 Pass@4 (8B, BFCL only, no std reported).
Full addition 40.83/62.00 vs selective addition 44.33/64.66.
Granularity ablation (8B/14B, ReMe fixed, BFCL).

gap.author_gap: Procedural memory is treated as passive append-only storage: coarse trajectory-level entries, retrieved experiences applied without adaptation, and no timely update/removal so pools degrade into valid insights plus toxic noise.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and partly evidenced by this paper's own ablations (trajectory- vs keypoint-level; full vs selective addition). The statement that prior methods neglect removal is overstated: other contemporaneous memory systems with pruning/consolidation are not discussed.

claims.text: ReMe establishes a new state of the art in agent memory systems on BFCL-V3 and AppWorld.
claims.setting: Qwen3-8B/14B/32B, three runs; BFCL 150 eval tasks, AppWorld test-normal 168
claims.baseline_control: No Memory, A-Mem, LangMem (author re-implementations with prompt modifications, retrieve-once protocol)
claims.selection_vs_test: fixed pool built from training split; dynamic pool updated on the evaluation stream
claims.result_denominator: 8B avg Avg@4 27.65 (none) / 27.09 / 27.79 / 30.78 (fixed) / 34.94 (dynamic); similar ordering for 14B and 32B
claims.allowed_conclusion: Against these re-implemented baselines ReMe(fixed) and ReMe(dynamic) are best on both benchmarks with Qwen3 sizes; baseline fidelity and dynamic-stream protocol limit the SOTA wording.

claims.text: Memory-scaling effect: Qwen3-8B with ReMe outperforms memoryless Qwen3-14B.
claims.setting: Table 1 averages over BFCL and AppWorld
claims.result_denominator: Pass@4 avg 55.03 vs 54.65 (+0.38); Avg@4 avg 34.94 vs 35.62 (-0.68); BFCL Avg@4 45.17 vs 48.66 (lower), AppWorld Avg@4 24.70 vs 22.57 (higher)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Only 14B+ReMe over 32B-none holds on both averaged metrics; 8B>14B holds on AppWorld and on averaged Pass@4 by 0.38, not on Avg@4 or on BFCL.

claims.text: Each refinement component (selective addition, failure-aware reflection, utility-based deletion, rerank, rewrite) contributes.
claims.selection_vs_test: same eval set, no pool-evolution split reported
claims.allowed_conclusion: Selective addition is clearly better than full addition; reflection/deletion effects are small or noise-level on Avg@4 and shown on one model/benchmark without std.
Fine-grained extraction helps in this setting; Avg@4 gaps are small relative to run std.

claims.text: ReMe generalises across backbones and BFCL categories.
claims.setting: six additional LLMs on BFCL; other BFCL categories with pool from 50 base tasks
claims.allowed_conclusion: Consistent gains over no-memory on BFCL with several backbones/categories (single benchmark family).

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A pool built from separate training tasks (ReMe-fixed) improves Qwen3-8/14/32B over no-memory and two re-implemented memory baselines on BFCL-V3 (150 tasks) and AppWorld test-normal (168), with 3-run std; granularity and addition-strategy choices matter; online refinement helps further but is entangled with test-stream exposure (author_report).
cannot_say: 8B+ReMe > 14B in general (holds only on averaged Pass@4 by 0.38)
utility-based deletion is critical (Avg@4 +0.17 within noise, no std)
gains survive matched budget incl. reflection retrials
unresolved: dynamic-variant task order and trial sharing
assessment.note: author_report only; no reproduction or our_run.
